nudge_table.reason: vocal_belief -14: lead vocal is masked — hold the level and width pushes until the masking clears; the voice comes forward by opening the field around it, then it sits on top and loud
vocal_belief -6: stereo image is already width-crowded — more width trades the forward punch for size

promotion_table.reason: loop_promotion +4.0: a foregrounded/dominating loop — commit to it and drive it forward as the record's energy (source material respected) rather than leaving it static

conservative.bias: commit to the mix in front of you, forward and present; the thinning-out moves are withheld

front_and_center.bias: the lead vocal front and center, present and loud; the record is built up around the voice

commit_and_slam.bias: commit early, print the energy, mix into the bus — loud, dense and forward from the first pass

drum_slam.bias: punchy forward drums, parallel-crushed for impact; the kit slams and fills the floor

big_chorus.bias: section contrast and impact through energy — the chorus lands bigger than the verse

experimental.bias: aggressive saturation and crushed energy, the mix pushed past polish into impact

philosophy: A mix is finished when it hits: the lead vocal sits on top and loud, the drums punch forward, the low end drives with weight, and every section commits — the chorus lands bigger than the verse and the energy never lets up. The record is dense and present, filled rather than carved, and it carries the same impact on every system it plays back on.
aesthetic_kill_switches: Never chase reference loudness at the mix stage.
Never widen the full mix to solve chorus lift.
Never make the lead vocal less intelligible unless explicitly approved.
Never allow a stock loop to dominate the song identity by accident.
Never let the lead vocal fall under the wall of energy — the voice stays on top and loud.
Never let the drums go soft where the section needs to hit — the kit carries the impact.
Never trade the punch of the low end for a polished but lifeless bottom.
Never thin the record out to sound clean — density and commitment come first.
